title: The magma automorphism group of a cyclic group twisted by a transposition is trivial unless the transposition is the inversion
author: Nigel P. Byott, Edgar Jasko
work: Magma Automorphisms and Quasi-Linear Cycle Sets
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 3.2 of the article (source label trans-thm, source0.tex lines 550--558): for the cyclic group of order n greater than two and a transposition tau = (ab) with gcd(b-a,n) = 1, the group of magma automorphisms fixing tau is trivial when b is not equal to minus a and equals the two-element group generated by the inversion when b equals minus a, which also settles the conjecture of the paper in that case. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 60-line proof at source0.tex lines 559--618. H2: the proof is an original structural computation rather than a qualifying examination exercise: the solver must first dispose of the small cases by a coprimality argument, then use the permutation-theoretic normal form of the magma automorphism group supplied by the delivered context to reduce the problem to the study of a single inversion-like symmetry, and finally show that no further automorphism can fix the transposition. That reduction of a magma-theoretic symmetry group to an explicit two-element group is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
